$comment: Three custom product pages for EconByte 1.1, text only. Prepared locally in plan Task 6a; no App Store Connect call was made. Design section 13.4 requires each page to use only its matching screenshots and claims, and Apple's rules cap a version at 35 custom product pages with up to 3 localizations each - these are en-US only.
createAfter: version 1.1 is APPROVED (design section 13.4). Creating them earlier would point campaigns at a page whose build does not exist yet.

sharedRules.attribution: Campaign links must carry a unique ct value per page and the numeric Apple provider token pt. A download without the numeric provider token is unattributed; campaign lift is never claimed from impressions or downloads alone (design section 13.4).
sharedRules.providerToken: OWNER ITEM - the numeric pt value comes from the Apple Search Ads / provider record and is not stored in this repository.

pages.name: Economics in five minutes
pages.intent: habit and microlearning searches - 'learn economics', 'daily learning', 'five minute learning'
pages.promotionalText: One short set a day. Eight cards, plain language, a sourced example on the back of each one.
pages.description:
Economics, in the time it takes to make coffee.

EconByte gives you one set of eight cards a day. The front of each card explains a single concept in plain language. Flip it over for a real-world example and the institution and document it came from. Finish the set, keep your streak, and save anything you want to read again.

- 120 cards across 15 topics, eight cards per topic
- Inflation and Interest Rates are free; the other 13 topics open with one $0.99 purchase
- Bookmarks, streak and an optional daily reminder that stays off until you turn it on
- No account, and everything works offline

Educational content only. EconByte does not provide financial, investment or tax advice.
pages.screenshotNote: 05-session-complete.png is deliberately excluded, reconciling this page with the hold recorded in AppStore/1.1/screenshots/manifest.json (storefrontRecommendation.hold). The capture is dominated by the one-time analytics/diagnostics consent offer. The hold stands; the page uses the plain completion value carried by 06-home-streak.png instead.

pages.name: Inflation explained
pages.promotionalText: What inflation actually measures, why prices rose, and where the numbers come from. Free to read.
pages.description:
Why does the same grocery cart cost more?

EconByte's Inflation topic answers that in eight short cards - what inflation measures, how the Consumer Price Index is built, what core inflation strips out, and what a central bank can and cannot do about it. Every card's back carries a real-world example with the source it came from, such as the Consumer Price Index series published by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

- Inflation is one of the two topics that are free, with no account and no sign-up
- 15 topics and 120 cards in total; 13 topics open with one $0.99 purchase
- Read offline, bookmark what you want to keep

Educational content only. EconByte explains how prices are measured; it does not provide financial, investment or tax advice.

pages.name: Interest rates and your money
pages.intent: interest-rate, Federal Reserve and monetary-policy searches - policy literacy, not advice
pages.promotionalText: What a rate decision is, who makes it, and how it reaches borrowing and saving. Explained, not advised.
pages.description:
Understand a rate decision before it reaches the headlines.

EconByte's Interest Rates and Central Banks topics explain what a policy rate is, who sets it, how it travels through borrowing and saving, and what the yield curve is actually showing. Each card's back gives a real-world example with the institution and document behind it.

- Interest Rates is free to read; Central Banks, Fiscal Policy, Debt & Deficits and 10 more topics open with one $0.99 purchase
- 120 cards across 15 topics, eight per topic
- Optional daily reminder, bookmarks, offline reading, no account

Educational content only. EconByte explains policy; it does not provide financial, investment or tax advice, and it makes no claims about returns, rates you will receive, or outcomes.
